name: Brazil Red
lede: Brazil red is an old name for a red pigment, listed in an eighteenth-century scheme of red colorants.

sections.title: A red on a pigment list
sections.body:
In 1769 Jacob Christian Schäffer proposed a standard set of principal colors and gave the pigments for each [3]. For red his list read minium, cochineal, cinnabar, carmine, *kugellack*, Brazil red, Florentine lake and English red [3]. The books consulted say little more about it, so its chemistry is not stated here [3].

The name suggests a link to the dyewood of Brazil, but the sources read do not say so, and the article leaves that open [3].

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body: The swatch is a brick-like red, #B5402D, from Ridgway's color book and ISCC-NBS lists [4]. Its nearest named neighbors are Brick and Medium Carmine [4]. Compare [[red]], [[carmine]] and [[vermilion]] [4]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 44, chroma 59 and hue 38 degrees [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this red in 543 of 23,531 paintings, as photographed [2]. India accounts for 67 of them, and Albrecht Dürer for 9 [2]. These are photographs of varnished and aged surfaces [2]. The numbers say little about the pigment of the same name [2].
